passages.note: Campaign plan says to provide free voter ID cards and require identification for in-person voting; it does not say photo ID, names no affidavit fallback, and sets no ID number on mail ballots, so it shows the pro-ID side without separating rungs 2-4.
Debate remark 'I support voter ID in California' given in reply to a point about election integrity, not a question on ID type; it names no kind of ID or fallback.
Press release about speeding up the ballot count; it says nothing about how a voter's identity is verified.

rows.reasoning: His plan to 'require identification for in-person voting' with free voter ID cards, and his debate line 'I support voter ID in California', place him on the side that wants identification, but neither says photo ID, an affidavit fallback for voters without one, or 'an ID number on every mail ballot'. Nothing separates 'Accept non-photo identification', 'Require photo ID ... after signing an affidavit' and 'Require photo ID in person and an ID number on every mail ballot', so the row is BLANK.

quotes.text: Provide free voter identification cards to all registered voters and require identification for in-person voting.
That's why I support voter ID in California.
